verdict.main_explanation: The pure-gauge algebra and the failure of the naive mask on the declared centered patch are correct. The fixed 6-to-7 edge is not a boundary edge of the predecessor's anchored block B(0)=[0,12]^4. The supplied claim of source-compatible centered geometry and the anchor-to-boundary separation justification are not established and must not be retroactively sanitized.
verdict.supplement_explanation: The corrected anchored 12-to-13 witness is valid with the declared global exterior gauge condition. CMP96 II (2.3), read together with the explicit Omega0 extension in CMP99 Background, supplies direct primary evidence for typewise differences/complements. At k=1 the bond stratum is E(O) minus E(X), not E(O minus X), under the declared common point regions and native source blocks.
verdict.global_conclusion: The naive incidence lift of the point complement is ruled out as a reconstruction of the raw fine fixed-bond stratum in the corrected anchored setting. This is neither a refutation of a source theorem nor a completed identification of the physical conditional kernel, final gauge-fixed fiber, or normalized marked law.

verified_metadata.author: T. Balaban
verified_metadata.title: Spaces of regular gauge field configurations on a lattice and gauge fixing conditions

main_1753_findings.finding: Spaces (1.13) is a raw space of group-valued configurations with fixed scale-j means; (1.14) imposes pointwise identity at the mixed-scale site set. The associated invariance statement is explicitly before the later averaged-gauge modification.
main_1753_findings.consequence: A test of this raw point-gauge space is logically distinct from an edge count after axial or Landau gauge fixing.

main_1753_findings.finding: The mean is not replaced by an invented average. Spaces p78 gives endpoint equivariance; Averaging p19 gives (11) and the actual definition (15). The unit field has mean I. A pure gauge supported away from all coarse representatives leaves every coarse mean I, since the values at both coarse endpoints are I.
main_1753_findings.proof: For U=I, U^u(a,b)=u(a)u(b)^(-1). Every path holonomy equals u(start)u(end)^(-1), every plaquette holonomy is I, and the covariant derivative/divergence of the constant identity curvature is zero. The logarithms in the mean of a closed holonomy are log I=0.
main_1753_findings.consequence: The curvature conditions (1.7)-(1.9) hold for every positive amplitude; sufficiently small nonzero t can satisfy any additionally required local chart neighborhood. The finite pi/3 phase witness does not itself assert a theorem-specific smallness threshold.

main_1753_findings.finding: All 24 listed loops were read and independently checked. They are distinct closed nearest-neighbor elementary plaquettes and exactly the full set incident to the support site in d=4. Their integer phases recompute to zero; the selected edge phase recomputes to one.
main_1753_findings.consequence: This verifies flatness arithmetic, not source block membership or membership in an original RG sector.

main_1753_findings.finding: The inherited source blocks are anchored: B(y) has y_mu <= z_mu < y_mu+L in fine units. CMP98 (2) and CMP95 I (1.6) agree. No conversion to blocks centered at the coarse representative was found in Spaces pp75-82 or the consulted geometric inheritance passages.
main_1753_findings.exact_issue: When 0 is the source coarse representative, B(0)=[0,12]^4. Both (6,1,0,0) and (7,1,0,0) lie in that block. Thus the frozen original edge is not a crossing edge, is not in E(O minus X) on this source patch, and cannot witness the claimed source-compatible loss of its fine fixed datum.
main_1753_findings.nuance: The same algebra is valid in the separately stipulated centered patch [-6,6]^4. An explicitly declared coordinate recentering would also shift the source coarse lattice and block representatives. Such an unprovided re-identification must not be silently inserted into the frozen input, nor identify old anchors with physical block centers.
main_1753_findings.consequence: The literal main-input source-geometric realization is not accepted. The separate corrected witness does not retroactively validate it.

main_1753_findings.finding: The center-distance argument is not valid for the old anchored source convention. In B(0)=[0,12]^4, z=(12,0,0,0) is a nonrepresentative inside site and w=(13,0,0,0) is the neighboring exterior coarse representative; they are one fine step apart.
main_1753_findings.consequence: The assertion that an interior free site cannot neighbor an exterior constrained representative cannot be transferred to this source. The after-lift fine mask has a different valid justification: every fixed fine bond under that mask has neither endpoint in X. It does not require the false separation claim.

main_1753_findings.finding: Whenever an actual crossing bond has an unconstrained endpoint x in X, an endpoint y in O minus X, and x is not a constrained coarse representative, E(O minus X) fixes that bond while the stipulated point-site gauge permits u_t(x) nontrivial.
main_1753_findings.proof: U^u(x,y)=diag(exp(it),exp(-it)) is not I for 0<t<pi. The incidence lift fixes this coordinate because y belongs to the point ring. This contradicts invariance of that reconstructed raw space, even though the actual means remain equivariant.
main_1753_findings.consequence: The failure belongs to the naive reconstruction. It is not a counterexample to the source theorem and does not require x to be a surviving final gauge-fixed coordinate.

main_1753_findings.finding: A lone 13-block is not shown to satisfy the source M1 and R conditions, and making a centered picture larger does not change its representative convention. The local algebra is independent of M1. A correctly anchored patch can be embedded in arbitrarily large admissibly aligned boxes; this is justified separately for 1753S.
main_1753_findings.consequence: No original P0/P1/Q1 sector with U=I and proper X is inferred from geometric admissibility.

main_1753_findings.finding: For proper O, E(O) minus E(X) can contain a bond leaving O. The point restriction only on (O minus X) union I does not on its face constrain the far endpoint outside O. Therefore avoiding the inner-crossing defect does not alone prove invariance under every globally defined transformation satisfying only that displayed site restriction.
main_1753_findings.consequence: One must supply the relevant exterior support/boundary convention, or use O=T, before asserting global invariance. The main input's remaining-boundary obligation is material. This is a limitation of the proposed transfer, not an allegation that a source theorem is false. The actual test gauge, supported within X, has no exterior problem.

main_1753_findings.finding: Spaces p80 replaces point values by averaged restrictions and explains that these restrictions generally fail to form a group. Page81 states that the resulting final image Sigma_k need not lie in the original fixed-data space (1.13). Thus raw point-gauge invariance cannot be imported unchanged to the final section.
main_1753_findings.direct_check: For background I and the one-site diagonal gauge in an anchored L=13 block, Averaging (78) gives its block gauge average at the representative as diag(exp(it/13^4),exp(-it/13^4)). This is not I for 0<t<pi. Inverting the gauge only changes the sign. The same supported gauge therefore fails the final averaged restriction.
main_1753_findings.consequence: No final Landau-section, Jacobian, hard-propagator, eliminated-coordinate, or normalized-law result follows.

main_1753_findings.finding: The input's suggested falsifiers do not exhaust source-applicability objections. The source geometry can fail because the declared edge is not crossing, while x is still unconstrained and its transformed edge value is still nontrivial.
main_1753_findings.consequence: Source compatibility must be tested independently of the algebraic nonidentity. Requiring only an unchanged crossing value or a constrained x would miss the actual anchored-block objection.

original_finite_verification.finite_geometry_check_scope: Local membership only; the small illustrative containing box was not claimed to satisfy fixed source M1/R.

supplement_1753S_findings.finding: For B(0)=[0,12]^4 and x=(12,1,0,0), y=(13,1,0,0), the prescribed edge crosses the block face and x is not a coarse anchor. The gauge supported only at x is I on all of X^c and all coarse anchors. It satisfies the point-site restriction, preserves coarse means, and changes the naive fixed fine crossing datum.
supplement_1753S_findings.consequence: The corrected source-native local obstruction is valid. The additional exterior condition does not remove the offending gauge; it is already satisfied by this witness. Hence this is not an illicit restriction that evades the countertest.

supplement_1753S_findings.finding: CMP96 II p224 (2.3) expressly defines the differences and Lambda0=Omega1^c for sets of sites and sets of bonds. With incidence E, the bond complement is T_bonds minus E(X), not E(T_sites minus X). Background p393 says its geometric change is to start the sequence at Omega0 and gives the corresponding differences; Spaces (1.5), (1.12)-(1.13) uses this setting.
supplement_1753S_findings.exact_raw_binding: For common point regions Omega0=O and Omega1=X at k=1, Lambda0_sites=O minus X and Lambda0_bonds=E(O) minus E(X). The zero-step field average is the identity on its fine-link domain. The zero-step site/gauge operation has a different domain and is not to be conflated with it.
supplement_1753S_findings.consequence: This pays the typed raw fine-index identification in this common-region source setting. It is stronger than a uniqueness inference from gauge invariance alone, but does not reconstruct every source object or the physical model's different coarse map.

supplement_1753S_findings.finding: For X subset O, adjoining the old fixed exterior gives (E(O) minus E(X)) disjoint-union (T_bonds minus E(O)) = T_bonds minus E(X). Under u=I on X^c, every fine bond in this fixed set has both endpoints fixed by the gauge, so its value is preserved for arbitrary fixed exterior data V0.
supplement_1753S_findings.coarse_condition: Coarse fixed means additionally need the declared identity at every coarse representative. The supported witness meets this condition.
supplement_1753S_findings.boundary_limit: Background pp393-394 supplies Dirichlet/support structure for the relevant linear operators and gauge functions. This supports the importance of exterior conditions but is not automatically a complete proof that the bare nonlinear Spaces (1.14), read in isolation for proper O, supplies the same global completion.
supplement_1753S_findings.consequence: The raw coordinate partition is justified as a set identity and as an invariant fine-data extension under the explicitly declared subgroup. It is not a product parametrization of the already constrained or gauge-fixed fiber.

supplement_1753S_findings.construction: Work in fine-lattice units with L=13. Choose an integer m=n*M1 >=3 and X={0,...,L*m-1}^4, a union of source large cubes of side L*M1 and of anchored L-blocks. Let O={-q*M1,...,L*m+q*M1-1}^4 with integer q>R. It is a union of fine-scale cubes of side M1. Its collar distance in fine units is at least q*M1, hence exceeds R*M1. Use a sufficiently large compatible torus so these boxes do not wrap.
supplement_1753S_findings.patch: Choose a fine block with first anchor coordinate L*(m-1) and transverse anchor coordinates L*r, 1<=r<=m-2. Translating by that coarse anchor gives the exact local x=(12,1,0,0), y=(13,1,0,0) patch at a flat boundary face, preserving the anchor lattice.
supplement_1753S_findings.limit: This proves compatibility of the local corrected witness with arbitrarily large admissible block and separation parameters. It fixes no source numerical M1/R value, applies no propagator theorem, and proves no realization by the original first RG sector.

supplement_1753S_findings.finding: 1753S correctly leaves the original centered-geometry and anchor-distance defects intact. It also retains the distinction between the raw source index, the physical block convention and mean, and the final averaged-gauge section.
supplement_1753S_findings.consequence: Acceptance of 1753S is local to its anchored countertest, typed raw-index definition, and explicitly stated exterior comparison. It is not approval of the main input as written or of the historical/master summary as a whole.
